open_questions: Gaia RUWE 1.706 indicates astrometric excess noise; RUCM log_p -0.1346 and RV amplitude 4.696 need RV follow-up to rule out a bound stellar companion despite no secondary eclipse.

Rotation amplitudes 2794 ppm (4.394 d) and 3542 ppm (3.027 d) are very large for Teff 3455 K and signal_over_rotation ~3.37; spot evolution could affect depth and shape and should be checked with higher-precision photometry.
dossier.public_summary: A flat-bottomed 1.4-x10^-3 dip repeats every 12.5 days steadily across sectors on a nearby M dwarf, giving a 2.2 Earth-radius size with no odd/even difference or secondary eclipse. No nearby star within one pixel could cause it with a small eclipse, so a planet is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Planet-sized 2.2 Rearth is below any stellar/brown-dwarf threshold; undiluted depth 1539 ppm on M dwarf (TIC rad 0.5144 Rsun) is consistent with planet, not a star.
Strongly flat-bottomed (negative V sigma) transit favours a whole planetary disc over a V-shaped grazing or small-star eclipse.

Depth steady in two sectors at 1429 and 1469 ppm (p_constant 0.8664) argues against a blended neighbour NEB with sector-dependent dilution; TIC contratio 0.05334 and neighbours plausible_within_1px 0 with closest that could at 26.3 arcsec needing 0.3004 eclipse disfavour blend.

No odd/even difference (depth_odd 1528 ppm vs depth_even 1249 ppm) and secondary snr 2.452 below detection; phase-curve amplitude 192 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.1314) small with chi2 7.729/9 also low, disfavouring an EB on target at twice the period.
Three individual transits (refit transits 3, SNR 14.62) are consistent with one depth (chi2 1.537/doF 2); it is not driven by a few bad events or noise.
